text:
The mechanism has substantial precedent. [HGN (KDD 2019)](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217) combines user-conditioned feature gates, instance gates, pooled recent-item representations, a long-term user embedding, and direct recent-to-candidate item products with separate input/output embeddings. [FPMC](https://www.ra.ethz.ch/cdstore/www2010/www/p811.pdf) combines persistent user preferences with factorized recent-item transitions; separate source/target factors already permit directionality. [SHAN](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2018/546) uses hierarchical attention to combine historical preferences and recent demand. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) itself adaptively selects history to capture short- and long-range dependencies. Assessment: a gated exponentially weighted last-five-item residual is plausibly a useful architectural variant, but these sources do not support claiming novelty for gated short-term preference modeling or directed transitions generally.

For pooled recent embedding r, a residual score contribution (g ⊙ Wr)ᵀe_candidate combines adaptive weighting and a potentially asymmetric transition map. This is not equivalent to HGN’s per-item hierarchical gates, but overlaps its pooled-interest and direct-transition mechanisms. With identity W and a constant gate, it reduces to a scaled recent-item dot-product term; exponential decay supplies a fixed positional preference rather than learned relevance. These are algebraic comparisons, not measured performance claims.

Recommended controls: SASRec alone; last-item residual; uniform last-five pooling; exponential last-five pooling; then a factorial comparison of identity versus learned W and fixed versus learned gates. Tune the fixed residual coefficient so gating cannot win merely by changing scale. Compare a learned global scalar with context-conditioned scalar/vector gates; compare unrestricted W with symmetric W and separate source/target embeddings. Sweep window length and decay, retraining each variant under identical seeds, sampling, optimization budgets, and pinned macro validation HR@10. These controls distinguish recency, pooling, scale, adaptive gating, and asymmetric projection.
